questions.q: Why does this lesson say four separate deliverables (eval dataset, monitoring setup, incident response plan, model card) are not yet a portfolio piece on their own?
options: A portfolio piece requires a connecting narrative — a problem, how it was verified, how you'd know if it broke, and what you'd do about it — not just four separate documents
Four deliverables are already a complete portfolio piece with nothing more needed
A portfolio piece must have at least ten separate documents to be valid
Deliverables can never be turned into a portfolio piece under any circumstances
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that the narrative connecting the four deliverables is what actually gets read and makes it a portfolio piece, not the documents in isolation.

questions.q: What does this lesson say is deliberately NOT part of the recommended five-minute capstone walkthrough?
options: A claim that the system is perfect and never fails
A description of the feature itself
The one chart from the monitoring setup
The incident response plan's failure mode
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly calls out that claiming perfection is left off the list, since showing a failed case and the resulting change is the stronger signal.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why is naming a specific limitation alongside the control that catches it a stronger statement than hiding the weakness or apologizing for it?
options: Because it demonstrates the actual discipline the course has been building — a process that finds flaws before a user does, not a system with no flaws
Because interviewers never care about limitations in any AI project
Because apologizing for weaknesses is required by every hiring process
Because hiding a weakness always results in a stronger presentation
questions.explain: The lesson frames specific, named limitations paired with the catching control as evidence of the exact skill the course has built, rather than a sign of failure.

questions.q: What does this lesson say this course (AI Security, Evaluation & Monitoring) closes, across its five chapters?
options: Nothing — this course is a standalone unit unrelated to any broader structure
Only the technical skill of writing Python code, with no connection to monitoring or governance
The risks (Ch.1), the evals (Ch.2), the monitoring (Ch.3), the governance (Ch.4), and one real pipeline built by the student (Ch.5)
A single chapter covering only incident response
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly summarizes all five chapters as the arc the course has built toward, culminating in the student's own built pipeline.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what course comes next in the AI Engineer path after this one, and what does it do differently?
options: AI Engineering Capstones — applying this same discipline at full scale across larger, more complete projects
Python for AI Engineering — starting the path over from the beginning
There is no next course; this is the final course in the entire path
Git & GitHub for Software Engineers — an unrelated foundational course
questions.explain: The lesson names AI Engineering Capstones as the next course, applying the same discipline at a larger scale than this course's single capstone project.
